pubchem.title: alpha-PHELLANDRENE
pubchem.description: Alpha-phellandrene is one of a pair of phellandrene cyclic monoterpene double-bond isomers in which both double bonds are endocyclic (cf. alpha-phellandrene, where one of them is exocyclic). It has a role as a volatile oil component, an antimicrobial agent and a plant metabolite. It is a cyclohexadiene and a phellandrene.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Alpha-phellandrene is a cyclic monoterpene, a type of volatile aromatic molecule that helps give certain plants their distinctive fresh, herbaceous scents. You most likely encounter it in the kitchen when cooking with fragrant herbs and spices, or when smelling the sharp, clearing aroma of eucalyptus leaves.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is notably found in culinary herbs like dill and fennel, as well as rosemary and cardamom. It is also a key component in the essential oils of several eucalyptus species.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to alpha-phellandrene for its broad biological activity, particularly its potential as an antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory agent. The strongest evidence so far comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b), which have prompted scientists to explore how this volatile oil might interact with human cells. Current investigations are looking into its ability to modulate immune responses and its effects on cellular health, including early tests on tumor cell lines.

structure_function.statement: Alpha-phellandrene is being studied for its potential to support the body's natural defenses against microbes.
structure_function.basis: This is based on 27 papers, including human observational research and in vitro microbial sensitivity tests.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward this molecule having antioxidant properties that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether alpha-phellandrene can influence apoptosis, or programmed cell death, in abnormal cells such as those in colon cancer models.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial measuring tumor markers and cellular apoptosis rates in patients receiving alpha-phellandrene as an adjunct therapy over six months.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating if this volatile compound could serve as an effective, natural insect repellent.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized controlled field trial comparing topical alpha-phellandrene formulations against standard synthetic repellents, measuring mosquito landing rates on human volunteers over an 8-hour period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward a potential role for alpha-phellandrene in managing depressive disorders, and researchers are curious if these mood-balancing effects will translate to humans.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A phase 1/2 double-blind, placebo-controlled human trial assessing mood scores and serum cortisol levels in adults with mild depression taking a standardized alpha-phellandrene extract for 8 weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: If early animal models bear out, alpha-phellandrene might help protect neurons from inflammatory damage, which researchers are actively testing in models of Parkinson's disease.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind clinical trial evaluating motor function and inflammatory biomarkers in early-stage Parkinson's patients receiving alpha-phellandrene alongside standard care for 12 months.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) for its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties, with the remainder of the research consisting of animal models and in vitro studies.

evidence: Measured in 2 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.05–0.11% of total volatiles (0.01–0.022mg per chew).
